title: United States bans imports of Russian oil and gas
body:
On 8 March 2022, United States President Joe Biden announced at the White House a ban on imports of Russian oil and gas, along with other Russian energy imports, in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The decision followed appeals by Ukrainian officials and others for the West to cut Russian energy revenue. The United States also imported a negligible amount of coal from Russia.

In 2021 the United States had imported about 20.4 million barrels per month of crude and refined products from Russia on average, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. That amounted to roughly 8 percent of U.S. liquid fuel imports. Benchmark Brent crude rose 5.4 percent to 129.91 dollars a barrel on the news. According to the motorists' association AAA, the average U.S. retail gasoline price reached 4.173 dollars per gallon early on 8 March, an all-time record.

The United Kingdom separately announced on the same day that it would phase out imports of Russian oil and oil products by the end of 2022. Russian oil products made up about 8 percent of British demand. Europe, which depended much more heavily than the United States on Russian energy supplies, did not join the American import ban at that time.
